questions.prompt: A line crosses two parallel lines. One angle is 65°. What is its corresponding angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles (the F shape) are equal, so it is 65°. 115° would be the angle on the same straight line.

questions.prompt: Alternate angles between parallel lines are...
questions.explanation: Alternate angles (the Z shape) are equal. It is co-interior angles that add up to 180°.

questions.prompt: Two co-interior angles lie between parallel lines. One is 100°. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles (the C shape) add up to 180°: 180 - 100 = 80. They are not equal, so 100° is wrong.

questions.prompt: A triangle has angles of 50° and 60°. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: 50 + 60 = 110 and 180 - 110 = 70. 110 is only the sum of the two angles you know.

questions.prompt: A triangle has a right angle and an angle of 30°. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: A right angle is 90°. 90 + 30 = 120 and 180 - 120 = 60. Forgetting the right angle gives 150°.

questions.prompt: Can a triangle have angles of 90°, 60° and 40°?
options: Yes, because one of them is a right angle
Yes, because each one is less than 180°
No, because they add up to 190°
questions.explanation: The three angles of a triangle must add up to exactly 180°. 90 + 60 + 40 = 190, which is too much.
